clue.text: Humorous writer's bloomer on day before start of troubles

indicators.note: on means the flower comes placed upon, so after, the day in the answer

parts.note: Sat is the standard abbreviation for Saturday
a bloomer here is a flower, and the iris is one

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, so only the opening of troubles is used

explanation.surface: A comic author's blunder on the eve of some trouble breaking out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a gaffe but is a flowering plant; 'on' and 'before' just place the pieces in order.
explanation.definitionFit: A satirist mocks follies through humour, so is a writer whose work is meant to amuse while it bites.

clue.text: Housemaster goes about checking uniform

indicators.note: to go about is to turn round, so the held letters are read backwards
checking means holding back or containing, so the word Housemaster holds the letters needed

explanation.surface: A school housemaster does his rounds, inspecting pupils' uniforms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'checking' signals letters held inside Housemaster (EMAS), and 'goes about' turns them round.
explanation.definitionFit: Uniform as an adjective means unvarying, identical throughout, which is the sense of being alike in every case.

clue.text: Do what's required, but complete form somewhat overzealously?

definitions.meaning: the idiom means to satisfy every requirement or expectation
literally, marking every option on a paper form, more than anyone asked for

explanation.surface: Meeting the brief, yet filling in a questionnaire with excessive eagerness.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for meeting every criterion comes from checklists where each item gets a mark when satisfied.

clue.text: Snubbing tips from architect, weirdly denigrates new plan

indicators.note: weirdly suggests the letters of denigrates are strangely jumbled
snubbing means rejecting, so the architect's tips are left out of the jumble
the tips of a word are its two end letters, here taken from architect

explanation.surface: An architect ignored, someone scornfully criticises a fresh scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snubbing' removes A and T (the 'tips from architect') from the letters of DENIGRATES; 'weirdly' rearranges what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: To redesign is to draw up a fresh plan for something, so the definition is a phrase giving the verb's sense.

clue.text: First thing for Harvard students' union, apparently

indicators.note: apparently says the answer, read as an instruction, only seems to produce the union's letters

parts.note: the UK National Union of Students is NUS; three letters written upwards in a down entry, so a sun going up gives them

explanation.surface: An American college's student body is first on the scene.
explanation.walkthrough: A cryptic indication: NUS (the UK National Union of Students) entered going up a down light reads as the answer. 'for Harvard' marks the definition as American usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunup is the American word for dawn, the first thing in the day, hence 'for Harvard' signalling US usage.

clue.text: Good feasts regularly finish with a port

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of Good feasts, here the second, fourth and so on

explanation.surface: Fine banquets routinely end with a glass of port wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' looks like the drink after a feast; it is a harbour city. 'finish with' puts A at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Odessa is a major Black Sea harbour city in Ukraine, so it is an example of a port.

clue.text: Fellow has clean home

parts.note: to dust is to clean by wiping away dirt
in means at home

explanation.surface: A man owns a spotless house.
explanation.definitionFit: Dustin is a man's first name, as in the actor Dustin Hoffman, so a fellow is defined by example.

clue.text: Foreign visitors can't see where to pause on trips

indicators.note: foreign means alien or strange, so the letters of visitors can't see are made strange by rearranging them

explanation.surface: Tourists from abroad cannot spot the places to stop on a road journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foreign' looks like it describes the visitors but is the anagram signal; the apostrophe in 'can't' is ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: Motorway rest areas with fuel, food and toilets are where drivers break long journeys.

clue.text: Source of poison dart is, I fancy, a leafy plant

parts.note: an asp is a venomous snake, a source of poison

indicators.note: fancy as an adjective means elaborate or fanciful, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone imagines a toxic dart coming from a leafy plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Source of poison' looks like a first-letter pick but is a whole word, the snake; 'fancy' rearranges DART IS I into IDISTRA.
explanation.definitionFit: The aspidistra is a tough foliage houseplant with large broad leaves, so is a leafy plant.

clue.text: Work of art is finished —- revolutionary, I held

indicators.note: held means the letter I is kept inside the other pieces

parts.note: something finished is over and past
Che Guevara is the crossword's favourite revolutionary

explanation.surface: An artwork is complete, a rebel declares, while being held.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastiche is an artistic piece imitating the style of another artist or period.

clue.text: Country club put on first class turns

parts.note: a mace is a heavy club used as a weapon
to don is to put on clothes

indicators.note: turns means the first-class abbreviation is reversed

parts.note: A1 means first class; the 1 is read as the letter I

explanation.surface: A golf club's top-tier members change direction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns' reverses AI, written for A1 with the digit as I, into IA.
explanation.definitionFit: North Macedonia, long known simply by the shorter name, is a nation in the Balkans.

clue.text: Take off … and land here

definitions.meaning: to take off clothes is to undress
an airstrip is a place where aircraft land

explanation.surface: Aircraft departure and touchdown at a runway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take off' tempts as the aircraft sense to pair with landing; it means undress.
explanation.definitionFit: Undressing is stripping, and a landing strip is a runway for aircraft, two unrelated senses.

clue.text: Singer runs out of money

indicators.note: out of means the runs letter is taken away from the money word

parts.note: brass is British slang for money
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A vocalist has spent all her cash.
explanation.definitionFit: A bass is a male voice of the lowest range, and so a type of singer.

clue.text: Frightened animal that is behind tree, turning to head for ditch

indicators.note: behind means the that-is abbreviation comes after the tree

parts.note: a pet is a tame animal

indicators.note: turning means the tree word is read backwards

parts.note: the fir is a conifer
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, taken from ditch

explanation.surface: A scared creature hides behind a tree, then heads for a ditch.
explanation.definitionFit: Petrified literally means turned to stone, and figuratively frozen with fear, terrified.

clue.text: Another disaster during month for athlete

indicators.note: during means the rearranged letters sit within the month

parts.note: Mar is the abbreviation for March

indicators.note: a disaster is a wreck, so the letters of Another are wrecked and rearranged

explanation.surface: Yet another calamity strikes during the month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disaster' looks like the subject of the surface but is the anagram signal; 'during' places the result inside the month.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-distance runner who competes over twenty-six miles is one kind of athlete.

clue.text: Loyalty such as union inspires

indicators.note: inspires is read literally as breathes in, so the union takes the for-example letters inside

parts.note: an alliance is a union of parties
e.g. stands for exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: Fidelity is the kind of thing a trade union stirs up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inspires' is read literally as breathes in, so the union takes the example abbreviation inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Allegiance is faithful loyalty owed to a ruler, nation or cause.

clue.text: Wife's left a bowl containing meat on top of everything else

indicators.note: containing means the shortened bowl holds the meat inside it
left means the wife's letter has departed from a bowl

parts.note: veal is calf meat

explanation.surface: A wife has gone, leaving a bowl holding meat on top of everything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wife's left' means wife has left, so W departs; 'containing' then wraps what remains around the meat.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means more than anything, especially, said of what matters most in addition to all else.

clue.text: America backs one foreign version of The Godfather?

indicators.note: backs means America comes at the back, after the foreign word

parts.note: a stage French or German accent says 'the' as 'ze'

explanation.surface: The US funds a foreign remake of the Mafia film The Godfather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Godfather' looks like the film title; split it so 'The' is accent fodder and 'Godfather' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this deity is father of gods and men, so is literally a god who is a father.

clue.text: Colour fit for use in felt-tip perhaps

indicators.note: for use in means the fitting word is put inside the pen

parts.note: a felt-tip is an example of a pen
to agree is to fit or match, as accounts agree

explanation.surface: A shade suitable for a felt-tip pen.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a bright yellowish green, the shade of fresh garden peas.

clue.text: One might be probed by hospital

definitions.text: One might be probed by hospital

indicators.note: probed by means the hospital letter goes into the one word

parts.note: an ace is the one in a suit of cards
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A pain that doctors at a hospital might investigate.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: a persistent pain is something hospital staff might probe.
explanation.definitionFit: A pain is the sort of complaint a clinic examines, so the whole clue describes it.

clue.text: Aussie singer, individual with yen to have warmer clothing

indicators.note: clothing means the heater wraps around the other pieces

parts.note: a heater warms a room
one means a single individual
Y is the abbreviation for the Japanese yen

explanation.surface: An Australian vocalist, single and longing, wears something warm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'singer' is a songbird, not a vocalist.
explanation.definitionFit: These nectar-feeding songbirds are found chiefly in Australia, so an Aussie singing bird.

clue.text: Fish — portion of it served with bread

parts.note: 'it' refers back to the fish, and a fin is part of a fish
naan or nan is a flat Indian bread

explanation.surface: A piece of fish is served with some bread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' points back to 'Fish', whose fin is a portion of it. Finnan is smoked haddock, from Findon near Aberdeen.
explanation.definitionFit: Finnan haddock is cold-smoked haddock from north-east Scotland, so a fish as eaten.

clue.text: Scottish chap's brief report about journey

parts.note: he refers to a chap

indicators.note: about means the shortened report goes around the journey
brief means the report word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: a bang is a loud report, like a gunshot
a ride is a journey

explanation.surface: A Scotsman's short account of a trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'report' is a loud noise, not an account; 'brief' cuts BANG to BAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hebrides are islands off western Scotland, so belonging to them is Scottish.

clue.text: Snack not available, cut short

indicators.note: cut short means the chop word loses its last letter

parts.note: to chop is to cut

explanation.surface: A snack is unavailable, the supply reduced.
explanation.definitionFit: A tortilla chip with toppings is a Mexican-style snack food.

clue.text: Is this just the thing in centre of Agen?

definitions.text: Is this just the thing in centre of Agen?

indicators.note: in means the thing goes inside the centre letters
the centre of a word is its middle letters, here of Agen

parts.note: it means the perfect thing, as in 'this is it'

explanation.surface: A holidaymaker wonders whether a house in central Agen is ideal.
explanation.walkthrough: Agen is a town in south-west France, where such rented holiday homes are common.
explanation.definitionFit: A French holiday cottage is exactly what one might rent in the middle of a town like Agen.

clue.text: Head's spinning in shock

indicators.note: spinning means the head word is read backwards

parts.note: nut is slang for head, and 's adds S

explanation.surface: A person's head reels in shock.
explanation.definitionFit: To shock someone senseless is to daze or stupefy them, a verb sense.

clue.text: Former president and vain emperor had this?

definitions.meaning: in The Emperor's New Clothes the vain ruler wore nothing; 'nix' is slang for nothing, so nothing on

explanation.surface: A past president and a conceited emperor share a trait.
explanation.walkthrough: The vain emperor of the fairy tale wore nothing at all, so read the answer split in two.
explanation.definitionFit: The 37th US president, who resigned over Watergate, is an obvious former president.

clue.text: Philosopher gets to party but is denied entry … thus?

definitions.text: Philosopher gets to party but is denied entry … thus?

parts.note: John Locke was an English philosopher
a do is a party

indicators.note: denied entry means the word but loses its first letter, its way in

explanation.surface: A thinker arrives at a party only to be turned away at the door.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the result too: barred from entering, a person is left outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Being refused entry and kept outside a shut door is the plain sense of the phrase.

clue.text: Insurrection is welcomed by group operating illegally

indicators.note: welcomed by means the word is goes inside the ring

parts.note: a ring is a criminal gang, as in a smuggling ring

explanation.surface: A revolt gets support from a criminal gang.
explanation.definitionFit: A rising is a revolt or uprising against authority, a noun sense.

clue.text: Picks fight with plump boy

parts.note: round means plump, chubby
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: Someone starts a brawl with a chubby lad.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn on someone suddenly and attack them verbally is to pick a fight with them.
